questions.question: The aim of the Permanent Settlement Act of 1793 was to enter into an agreement for fixed revenue collection between the East India Company and _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Landlords**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Permanent Settlement Act of 1793 was introduced by the British East India Company under the leadership of Lord Cornwallis.
 
• This act aimed to create a fixed revenue system by entering into agreements with landlords (Zamindars) for revenue collection.
 
• The landlords were responsible for collecting taxes from the peasants and paying a fixed amount to the Company.
 
• It was intended to stabilize revenue collection and ensure a steady income for the British administration.
 
• Landlords were given hereditary rights over the land, which they could pass on to their descendants.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Zamindari System**

 
 
• The Zamindari System was a traditional system where landlords (Zamindars) collected taxes from peasants.
 
• Under this system, Zamindars were recognized as landowners by the British government.
 
• The system aimed to create a class of loyal landlords who would support British rule.
 
 
 
• **Revenue Settlement**
 
 
• Revenue Settlement refers to the agreement made between the British government and landlords for tax collection.
 
• It ensured that the government received a fixed amount of revenue annually.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Peasants**
 
 
• Peasants were often exploited as landlords sought to maximize revenue collection.
 
• Many peasants faced high taxes and were at risk of losing their land.
 
 
 
• **Permanent Settlement Act**
 
 
• The act was part of the larger framework of British colonial administration in India.
 
• It laid the foundation for the modern land revenue system in Bengal and later extended to other parts of India.

questions.question: Identify the crop which is grown in Rabi season in North India from the following.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gram**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Gram, also known as chickpea, is a major crop grown in the Rabi season in North India.
 
• Rabi crops are sown in winter from October to December and harvested in summer from April to June.
 
• Gram is a leguminous crop and is a rich source of protein, making it an important part of the diet in India.
 
• It is predominantly grown in the states of Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, and Maharashtra.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rabi Crops**

 
 
• Rabi crops, also known as winter crops, are sown in the winter season and harvested in the summer.
 
• These crops require a relatively cool climate during the growing season and a warm climate during the harvesting period.
 
• Examples of Rabi crops include wheat, barley, mustard, and peas.
 
 
 
• **Kharif Crops**
 
 
• Kharif crops, also known as monsoon crops, are sown at the beginning of the rainy season and harvested at the end of the monsoon.
 
• These crops require a lot of water and hot weather to grow.
 
• Examples of Kharif crops include rice, maize, cotton, and millets.
 
 
 
• **Leguminous Crops**
 
 
• Leguminous crops belong to the family Leguminosae and are known for their ability to fix atmospheric nitrogen.
 
• These crops have symbiotic relationships with Rhizobium bacteria in their root nodules.
 
• Leguminous crops are an important source of protein and include crops like peas, beans, lentils, and gram.

questions.question: Which of the following Fundamental Duties is mentioned first in the Constitution of India?

options.text: To uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India
To cherish and follow the noble ideals which inspired our national struggle for freedom
To defend the country and render national service when called upon to do so
To abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag and the National Anthem

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag and the National Anthem**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Fundamental Duties** were added to the Constitution of India by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976.
 
• These duties are listed in **Article 51A** under Part IV-A of the Constitution.
 
• The Fundamental Duties aim to promote a sense of discipline and commitment among citizens.
 
• The first duty listed is **to abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag and the National Anthem**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental Duties:**

 
 
• These duties are intended to serve as a constant reminder to citizens to observe a certain set of moral and ethical norms, which are essential for the well-being of the country.
 
• There are currently 11 Fundamental Duties enumerated in the Constitution.
 
• The idea of Fundamental Duties is inspired by the Constitution of the former Soviet Union.
 
• Although these duties are non-justiciable, they serve as a guide to the behavior of citizens and can be enforced through moral and social pressure.
 
 
 
• **42nd Amendment Act, 1976:**
 
 
• This amendment is also known as the "Mini-Constitution" due to the extensive changes it introduced.
 
• It added ten Fundamental Duties to the Constitution, which were based on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee.
 
• It also made significant changes to the Preamble, Directive Principles of State Policy, and the powers of the President and Governors.
 
• This amendment aimed to curb the excessive powers of the judiciary and enhance the power of the Parliament.
 
 
 
• **Article 51A:**
 
 
• Article 51A specifies the Fundamental Duties of the citizens of India.
 
• The duties encompass a broad range of activities including respecting national symbols, cherishing the noble ideals of the freedom struggle, promoting harmony, and safeguarding public property.
 
• Citizens are also expected to develop scientific temper and humanism, and to strive for excellence in their spheres of activity.
 
• One of the duties added later was to provide opportunities for education to children between the ages of six and fourteen years.

questions.question: According to Census of India 2011, which union territories have the lowest literacy rate?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dadra and Nagar Haveli**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Dadra and Nagar Haveli had the lowest literacy rate among the Union Territories as per the Census of India 2011.
 
• The literacy rate of Dadra and Nagar Haveli was recorded at 76.2%.
 
• In comparison, Chandigarh had a literacy rate of 86.05%, Lakshadweep had a literacy rate of 92.28%, and Andaman and Nicobar had a literacy rate of 86.27%.
 
• The literacy rate is a key indicator of the socio-economic progress of a region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Census of India**

 
 
• The Census of India is a decennial exercise conducted by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, India under the Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India.
 
• It provides a comprehensive account of the demographic, social, and economic profile of the country.
 
• The first census in India was conducted in 1872, and since then, it has been carried out every ten years.
 
• The Census of India 2011 was the 15th National Census since 1872 and the 7th census after independence.
 
 
 
• **Literacy Rate**
 
 
• The literacy rate is defined as the percentage of people who can read and write with understanding in a given language.
 
• It is an important indicator of the educational status of a population.
 
• Literacy has a significant impact on various socio-economic factors including employment, income levels, health, and overall quality of life.
 
• Higher literacy rates are often associated with better economic development and improved social outcomes.
 
 
 
• **Union Territories of India**
 
 
• India is divided into states and Union Territories (UTs).
 
• Union Territories are regions governed directly by the Central Government of India.
 
• As of 2021, India has 8 Union Territories: Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Chandigarh, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu, Lakshadweep, Delhi, Puducherry, Jammu and Kashmir, and Ladakh.
 
• Each Union Territory has its own unique cultural, demographic, and socio-economic profile.

questions.question: As per the Indus Water Treaty 1960, how much per cent water can India use from the river?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**20 per cent**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Indus Water Treaty (IWT) was signed between India and Pakistan on 19th September 1960, with the World Bank being a signatory as well.
 
• Under the treaty, India was allocated the unrestricted use of all the waters of the eastern rivers (Sutlej, Beas, and Ravi) while Pakistan was allocated the western rivers (Indus, Jhelum, and Chenab).
 
• India, however, is entitled to use 20% of the total water carried by the Indus river system for irrigation, power generation, and transport purposes.
 
• The treaty has been a successful example of conflict resolution between two countries sharing water resources.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indus Water Treaty (IWT)**

 
 
• The IWT is a water-distribution treaty between India and Pakistan, brokered by the World Bank. It was signed in Karachi on 19 September 1960 by then Prime Minister of India Jawaharlal Nehru and then President of Pakistan Ayub Khan.
 
• The treaty allocates the use of the river waters of the Indus basin between India and Pakistan. The basin comprises six rivers: the Indus, Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas, and Sutlej.
 
• The treaty gives India control over the waters of the three eastern rivers – the Beas, the Ravi, and the Sutlej, while Pakistan has control over the waters of the three western rivers – the Indus, the Jhelum, and the Chenab.
 
• The treaty allows India to use the water of the western rivers for limited irrigation use and unrestricted use for power generation, domestic use, and non-consumptive use like navigation, fish culture, etc.
 
 
 
• **Water Sharing**
 
 
• India is allowed to use 20% of the water from the western rivers for purposes such as irrigation, power generation, and transport. This amounts to around 3.6 million acre-feet (MAF) of water.
 
• The treaty specifies that the flow of the rivers shall not be obstructed by any party, ensuring a continuous supply of water to both countries.
 
 
 
• **Conflict Resolution**
 
 
• The IWT has a permanent Indus Commission with a commissioner from each country, which meets regularly to discuss and resolve any issues that arise.
 
• In case of disputes, the treaty outlines a process of arbitration which involves a neutral expert appointed by the World Bank.

questions.question: The Indian Vice President is elected by an electoral college comprising members of _______________.

options.text: Rajya Sabha, Lok Sabha and State Legislative Council
Rajya Sabha and State Legislative Assembly

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**both the houses of Parliament**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Vice President of India is elected by an electoral college consisting of members of both houses of Parliament: the Rajya Sabha and the Lok Sabha.
 
• The election is conducted in accordance with the system of proportional representation by means of a single transferable vote.
 
• The Vice President serves a term of five years but can be re-elected.
 
• To be eligible for the position of Vice President, a candidate must be a citizen of India, at least 35 years old, and qualified to be a member of the Rajya Sabha.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Electoral College**

 
 
• An electoral college is a body of electors chosen or appointed by a larger group, in this case, members of both houses of Parliament in India.
 
• The members of the electoral college vote to elect the Vice President of India.
 
 
 
• **Proportional Representation**
 
 
• Proportional representation is a voting system aimed at achieving a close match between the percentage of votes and the percentage of seats obtained by each party or group of candidates.
 
• This system ensures that minority groups have a chance of representation in the elected body.
 
 
 
• **Single Transferable Vote**
 
 
• The single transferable vote (STV) is a voting system designed to achieve proportional representation through ranked voting in multi-seat organizations or constituencies.
 
• Under STV, voters rank candidates in order of preference, and candidates are elected sequentially based on those preferences.
 
 
 
• **Role of the Vice President**
 
 
• The Vice President of India is the second-highest constitutional office in the country, after the President.
 
• The Vice President acts as the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha (Council of States).
 
• In the absence of the President, the Vice President assumes the duties and responsibilities of the President.

questions.question: Who is the first Indian singer to have perform at the Royal Albert Hall in London?

__
 
• **Lata Mangeshkar** is one of the most revered and celebrated playback singers in India.

• The Royal Albert Hall is one of the most prestigious concert halls in the world, known for hosting a variety of high-profile events and performances.
 
• Lata Mangeshkar's performance at the Royal Albert Hall is a testament to her international acclaim and the global recognition of her talent.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lata Mangeshkar**

 
 
• Born on September 28, 1929, in Indore, India, Lata Mangeshkar is widely regarded as one of the greatest and most influential vocalists in the history of Indian music.
 
• She has recorded songs in over a thousand Hindi films and has sung songs in over thirty-six regional Indian languages and foreign languages.
 
• Her career spans over seven decades, and she has received numerous awards, including the Bharat Ratna, India's highest civilian award.
 
• Lata Mangeshkar is often referred to as the "Nightingale of India" due to her melodious voice and significant contributions to Indian music.
 
 
 
• **Royal Albert Hall**
 
 
• Located in London, the Royal Albert Hall is a concert hall that was opened in 1871 by Queen Victoria in memory of her husband, Prince Albert.
 
• The hall is known for its distinctive architecture and has a seating capacity of approximately 5,272 people.
 
• It hosts a wide range of events, including classical concerts, rock and pop performances, ballet, opera, and charity events.
 
• The Royal Albert Hall has been associated with many notable performers and events, making it a symbol of cultural and musical heritage.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about cell is correct?

options.text: Powerhouse of a cell is plastid.
Cell is a functional unit of life.
Cell membrane of a cell is hard and rigid.

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Cell is a functional unit of life.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **cell** is the **basic structural, functional, and biological unit of all living organisms**. It is often referred to as the **building block of life**.
 
• All living organisms, from the smallest bacteria to the largest plants and animals, are composed of one or more cells, making it the **functional unit of life**.
 
• Cells carry out essential processes such as **metabolism, growth, reproduction, and energy transformation**.
 
• The cell theory, proposed by **Schleiden and Schwann**, states that all living organisms are made of cells and that the cell is the fundamental unit of structure and function in all organisms.
 
• The cell contains various organelles such as the **nucleus, mitochondria, endoplasmic reticulum, and ribosomes**, which perform specialized functions to sustain life.
 
• Cells are classified into two types: **prokaryotic cells** (e.g., bacterial cells) and **eukaryotic cells** (e.g., plant and animal cells).
 
• This fundamental characteristic of cells makes them the **functional unit of life**, as they are responsible for carrying out all life processes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Bacterial cell contains cellulose.**__

 __
 
• Bacterial cells do not contain **cellulose**. Instead, their cell walls are made up of **peptidoglycan**, a polymer consisting of sugars and amino acids.
 
• Cellulose is a major component of the cell walls of **plants**, not bacteria.
 
 
 
• **Powerhouse of a cell is plastid.**__
 __
 
• The powerhouse of the cell is the **mitochondria**, not plastid. Mitochondria generate **ATP**, the energy currency of the cell.
 
• **Plastids**, such as chloroplasts, are involved in **photosynthesis** and other functions in plant cells but are not responsible for energy production.
 
 
 
• **Cell membrane of a cell is hard and rigid.**__
 
 
• The **cell membrane** is a **flexible and semi-permeable structure** made of a phospholipid bilayer. It is not hard and rigid.
 
• It controls the movement of substances in and out of the cell and provides structural support to the cell.

questions.question: In which pair of states is Holi also celebrated as Dola Purnima?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**West Bengal and Odisha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Dola Purnima** is celebrated with great fervor in both **West Bengal and Odisha** during the festival of Holi.
 
• It is also known as **Dol Jatra** in these regions.
 
• The festival involves the worship of **Lord Krishna** and people participate in joyous processions carrying the idol of Krishna on decorated palanquins.
 
• It is marked by the **playing of colors**, singing, dancing, and various traditional rituals and customs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dola Purnima**

 
 
• Dola Purnima is celebrated on the full moon day in the month of Phalguna (February-March).
 
• It is a significant festival for the followers of Vaishnavism, a sect of Hinduism that worships Lord Vishnu and his incarnations, particularly Krishna.
 
• The festival signifies the arrival of spring and is also associated with agricultural activities, especially the harvesting of new crops.
 
• In Odisha, the festival includes a ritual known as **Melana**, where deities from various temples are brought together in a grand procession.
 
 
 
• **Holi**
 
 
• Holi is one of the major festivals of India and is celebrated with enthusiasm across the country.
 
• It is known as the "Festival of Colors" and signifies the victory of good over evil, the arrival of spring, and the end of winter.
 
• The festival is celebrated by smearing colors on each other, dancing, singing, and enjoying festive foods and drinks.
 
• Holi is celebrated over two days, starting with Holika Dahan (bonfire) on the night before and followed by the main day of playing with colors.

questions.question: Identify the iron and steel plant that was developed in collaboration with Germany.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rourkela**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Rourkela Steel Plant (RSP) was set up in collaboration with Germany in the 1950s.
 
• It is located in Rourkela, Odisha, and is the first integrated steel plant in the public sector in India.
 
• RSP was established with the assistance of the German companies Krupp and Demag.
 
• The plant was inaugurated in 1959 and has been a significant contributor to India's steel production capacity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Iron and Steel Industry in India**

 
 
• India has a rich history of iron and steel production dating back to ancient times.
 
• The modern iron and steel industry in India began in the late 19th century with the establishment of Tata Iron and Steel Company (TISCO) in 1907.
 
• Post-independence, India developed several public sector steel plants, including those at Bhilai, Durgapur, Rourkela, and Bokaro.

• He is considered a **liberal reformer** who introduced several progressive policies during his tenure.

• Lord Ripon is often referred to as the **Father of Local Self-Government in India** due to his efforts to decentralize administration and empower local municipalities.
